checks: Compared the frozen claim with dcde24475c7f190c §3, (8). Both interior hypotheses in the frozen statement give an admissible limiting chart. The compact set of allowed representatives in the second hypothesis lets the chosen sequence remain in the chart interior.

Compactness gives attained minima and the common local y-Lipschitz bound passes to the marginal. At each differentiability point, comparison with the marginal gives the Fréchet lower support in both variables. The little-o term in the y increment is also little-o in the joint increment, including y fixed.

Checked the shrinking-hull and null-set argument. A separating direction gives a uniform bound on ordinary directional derivatives outside the exceptional null set. Fubini on parallel lines and absolute continuity integrate it, and continuity gives it on the line through the point. The same argument proves Fréchet subgradient inclusion. Shrinking hulls give a closed graph.

A subsequence of minimizing parameters converges, continuity preserves its activity, and the ordinary gradients converge to the prescribed g. In one fixed joint chart the parameter components are exactly zero throughout, and a smooth change of parameter coordinates preserves zero.

overlap.comparison: The accepted quantile normal cone pertains to the energy maximizer on a deepest slice and gives conic combinations of cap normals. It does not give the joint-gradient lift for a general locally Lipschitz minimum.

readability: The conclusion selects an active parameter separately for each ordinary gradient limit. The frozen proof correctly uses a compact set of interior minimizing representatives rather than requiring every clipped tilt to be interior.
review_method: Independent cold read of the frozen statement and proof, followed by source and exact predecessor comparison. Exact rational checks supplement the proof when arithmetic is relevant.
summary: The differentiability-point argument gives one joint generalized gradient with all parameter coordinates zero at the same limiting minimizer.
